title: Acceptance Report
description: One calibration report, as emitted by scripts/acceptance_report.py: filled operator review sheets joined back to the scored discovery-result / match-result runs they were cut from, reduced to the measurements that say whether the rubric discriminates. It carries PRD 17's Human Acceptance Rate and nothing else; PRD 17's RFQ Conversion needs outcome data from the application layer and is not derivable here. It is a MEASUREMENT document: nothing in it feeds a score, so a report can never change score_version. See references/calibration-notes.md section 7 for the protocol and references/data-contract.md section 9.3 for the field notes.

report_kind.description: Document discriminator, so validate_output.py --schema auto can route this document without guessing.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema contract, e.g. "0.1.0".

score_version.$comment: Inlined rather than referenced from the shared BUILD-CONTRACT 3.7 definition, and deliberately narrower: every record a report aggregates was produced by a scorer, so "unscored" is invalid here, and a report over two rubric versions is refused outright (BUILD-CONTRACT 12.3 rule 4, INV-23).
score_version.description: The one scoring rubric every aggregated record was scored with.

skill_version.description: Version of the skill package that produced this document.

as_of.description: The date stamped onto this report (--as-of, or the latest as_of of the scored documents). Scripts never read the wall clock (INV-14).

by_qualified.description: Acceptance split by the rubric's qualified flag: the precision of the flag (qualified_true), what it misses (qualified_false), and the records it never judged (qualified_unknown). Three buckets, not two, because "unknown is not false" (BUILD-CONTRACT 3.2) - folding an absent or "unknown" flag into qualified_false would report a gap as a rejection in the one document whose job is to measure the flag.

by_score_band.description: One entry per scoring.config.json calibration.score_bands pair, in config order.

threshold_sweep.description: What each candidate cut-off would have returned, over the calibration.threshold_sweep range.

by_country.description: Acceptance per record country, "unknown" last. A match-result carries no country on its candidates, so a match report groups everything under "unknown".

by_reason_code.description: One entry per reason_code of the _common.REVIEW_REASON_CODES vocabulary, in vocabulary order, whether or not it occurred.

false_exclusions.description: Records the rubric excluded that an operator nevertheless accepted, ordered by record_id. A non-empty list is the most actionable thing this report produces: it names a hard filter or evidence bar that is throwing away business.

notes.description: Run-level notes, including the insufficient-sample warning and the standing statement of what this report does not measure.

extensions.description: Reserved for consumer-specific additions; never read by this package.

rate_value.description: A rate in [0, 1] rounded half-up to calibration.rate_decimals, or null when its denominator is zero. Null means "no number exists here", never zero (BUILD-CONTRACT 3.2).

group_block.description: One population and how an operator judged it. `unsure` is counted and reported but never folded into either side of acceptance_rate.

band_row.description: One score band and how an operator judged the records inside it.

sweep_row.description: What one candidate threshold would have returned, and how well it would have separated. Every count here is over the RETURNED records of the scored run(s) only; `recall` is the one field whose denominator reaches wider, and its description says so.

threshold.description: The candidate cut-off this row asks about. A row BELOW the run's own threshold_used is only measurable when the run returned its below-threshold records; a match run does not, and the report then says so in notes[].

n_at_or_above.description: Returned records whose score is >= threshold, reviewed or not. Denominator: the returned population.

reviewed_at_or_above.description: Of those, how many carry any verdict (accept + reject + unsure). Denominator: n_at_or_above.

accept.description: Returned records at or above the threshold that an operator accepted.

reject.description: Returned records at or above the threshold that an operator rejected.

precision.description: accept / (accept + reject) among the records at or above this threshold. Denominator: the DECIDED reviews at or above the threshold; `unsure` is in neither half. Null when nothing at or above it was decided.

recall.description: accept-at-or-above / EVERY accepted record in the report, excluded ones included. Denominator: all accepted records, because an accepted record the rubric excluded is a lead this cut-off would also have lost - it sits at or above no threshold. Null when the report carries no accepted record at all.

auc_block.description: One AUC measurement. `auc` and `reason` are mutually exclusive: a value carries reason null, and a null value carries the reason it could not be computed.

reason.description: Why `auc` is null, or null when it is not.

distinct_values.description: How many distinct values this number took across the whole returned population. calibration-notes.md section 3 found the two heaviest buyer dimensions resolving to 2 and 3 distinct values over 20 real companies: a dimension with one value cannot separate anything, whatever its weight.

reason.description: Why `auc` is null, or null when it is not.

distinct_values.description: How many distinct values this dimension took across the whole returned population.

discrimination_block.description: Does a higher score mean an operator is more likely to accept? Reported on the total score and on each dimension separately, because a rubric whose total discriminates can still be carried by one light dimension (calibration-notes.md section 3).

metric.description: Plain-language definition of the number, so a reader never has to guess which AUC this is.

country_row.description: One record country and how an operator judged it.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, or the literal "unknown" when the scored document carries no country.

reason_row.description: How often one reason_code was given, split by whether the record was returned or excluded.

false_exclusion.description: One record the rubric excluded and an operator accepted.

record_id.description: The buyer_id / seller_id of the excluded record.

company_name.description: Company name as the scored document carried it, or null when it carried none.

failed_rule_ids.description: The HF-nn ids that excluded the record, in document order; empty for a query-fit or evidence-bar exclusion.

reason_code.description: The reason_code the operator gave, if any.

report_summary.description: The headline block: how much of the run was reviewed, and what the Human Acceptance Rate came out as.

source_kind.description: Which run shape was aggregated. A report never mixes the two.

threshold_used.description: The cut-off in force in the scored run(s), or null when they disagreed.

threshold_mode.description: The threshold mode in force, or null when the runs disagreed.

min_sample.description: The accept+reject floor below which this report refuses to be evidence (scoring.config.json calibration.min_sample, or --min-sample).

insufficient_sample.description: True when accept + reject is below min_sample. A true here means notes[] carries the line saying this report cannot justify a weight or threshold change.
